narrator: Lucy Westenra (diary and memorandum), Dr. Seward (diary), Pall Mall Gazette reporter (interview); telegram from Van Helsing
summary: Lucy sleeps peacefully with the garlic. On 13 September Mrs. Westenra, thinking the smell harmful, has removed the garlic and opened the window; Lucy is again drained, Van Helsing breaks down in despair, locks the door and transfuses her himself, then forbids anyone to move the flowers. Lucy enjoys four peaceful nights and a box of garlic arrives daily from Haarlem. The Pall Mall Gazette interviews zoo keeper Thomas Bilder: the wolf Bersicker escaped after a tall thin man with a hooked nose, pointed beard, red eyes and sharp teeth visited and stroked him; Bersicker returns by himself with cut head and broken glass. On 17 September Renfield bursts into Seward's study with a dinner-knife, cuts his wrist and licks the blood, shouting that the blood is the life. Van Helsing's telegram, misdirected to Carfax, Sussex, arrives 22 hours late. That night a wolf smashes Lucy's window, her mother tears off the garlic wreath and dies of fright, a cloud of specks blows in, the maids are drugged with laudanum in sherry, and Lucy is left alone with the dead.

scenes.title: Lucy sleeps with garlic
scenes.summary: Lucy finds comfort in the garlic and feels no fear of the flapping outside the window.
scenes.key_quote: I never liked garlic before, but to-night it is delightful!

scenes.title: Mrs. Westenra removes the garlic
scenes.location: Hillingham morning room, dining-room, Lucy's room
scenes.summary: Mrs. Westenra proudly says she removed the stuffy flowers and opened the window. Van Helsing weeps in despair in the dining-room, then locks Lucy's door and performs a third transfusion on his own arm.
scenes.key_quote: Devils or no devils, or all the devils at once, it matters not; we fight him all the same.

scenes.title: Four days of peace
scenes.summary: Lucy recovers; a boxful of garlic arrives daily from Haarlem; Van Helsing sleeps in a chair; bats nap against the panes.
scenes.key_quote: the boughs or bats or something napped almost angrily against the window-panes

scenes.title: The Escaped Wolf interview
scenes.location: Zoological Gardens, keeper's cottage behind the elephant-house
scenes.summary: Bilder describes the tall stranger who calmed the wolves and stroked Bersicker, the howling at moonrise and the broken cage. Bersicker returns by himself, head cut with broken glass.
scenes.key_quote: a tall, thin chap, with a 'ook nose and a pointed beard, with a few white hairs runnin' through it.

scenes.title: Renfield attacks Seward
scenes.summary: Renfield bursts in with a dinner-knife, cuts Seward's left wrist, is floored, and licks the spilt blood from the carpet.
scenes.key_quote: The blood is the life! The blood is the life!

scenes.title: Misdirected telegram
scenes.summary: Van Helsing's telegram, sent to Carfax, Sussex, arrives 22 hours late; Seward loses a night.
scenes.key_quote: Do not fail to be at Hillingham to-night.

scenes.title: The night the wolf came
scenes.summary: Lucy hears howling and a bat at the window; her mother joins her in bed; the window shatters and a gaunt grey wolf's head appears; Mrs. Westenra tears off the garlic wreath, points, and dies on top of Lucy.
scenes.key_quote: in the aperture of the broken panes there was the head of a great, gaunt grey wolf.

scenes.title: The drugged maids
scenes.summary: Lucy finds all four maids unconscious beside a decanter of sherry laced with laudanum from Mrs. Westenra's empty bottle, and returns to her dead mother, hearing the wolf's howl; lights burn blue and specks swirl.

puzzles.name: Keep the garlic in place
puzzles.setup: The household doesn't know why the garlic matters.
puzzles.obstacle: Mrs. Westenra removes it and opens the window.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing instructs her not to touch anything; the failure happens before the warning.
puzzles.game_idea: Defensive-time puzzle: use dialogue and notes to persuade NPCs not to disturb wards; ward integrity changes nightly.
puzzles.quote: she must not remove anything from Lucy's room without consulting him

puzzles.name: Which animal escaped and why
puzzles.setup: A wolf escaped and returned with cut head.
puzzles.obstacle: Link the stranger to Bersicker's escape.
puzzles.book_solution: Reporter interview yields description of the stranger, the moonrise howling and glass-cut head.
puzzles.game_idea: Interview-clue puzzle: bribe or befriend the keeper to extract the stranger's description.
puzzles.quote: I took a sort of mislike to him

puzzles.name: Who drugged the maids?
puzzles.book_solution: Lucy smells laudanum in the decanter and finds the medicine bottle empty.
puzzles.game_idea: Smell and inspect puzzle on a sideboard.

combat.name: Renfield's knife attack
combat.tactics: Seward keeps the table between them, Renfield is too quick, Seward punches him down.
combat.outcome: Seward's wrist cut; Renfield secured by attendants.
combat.game_idea: One-on-one encounter with a quick enemy; obstacle (table) grants dodge; ends with a bleeding status effect.
combat.quote: before I could get my balance he had struck at me and cut my left wrist rather severely

combat.name: Wolf at the window
